items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: as a result since I was 12 years old, when I was 12 I went on the road with Major Bowes.

ctx.x: Well let me tell you. I got thrown out of school for hitting a teacher. You read that. Right? I hit a teacher and unbeknownst to me the bandleader and the orchestra leader came to my house to tell my folks that if I came back and apologized to the teacher, the principal and the whole classroom that they were going to give me the scholarship to Juilliard as a snare drummer and tympanist. You know in school, when you get into the percussion section you start out with the triangle because there’s a tympanist who’s a…

Okay. Before we move on from this part of your life, sometimes you read that one of the reasons that bebop became a new style of jazz is that black musicians were trying to weed out the white imitators and that there was a racial component to this music. And I wondered what your observation was back at that time?
